claims.statement: The unweighted one-step subset-shadow result described in the route report does not, without an additional proved bridge, establish the selector-weighted deletion-plus-two-for-one cut inequalities.
claims.scope: Narrowed application check only: the mismatch between subset-shadow cardinality and absent-vertex switch outputs / selector-dependent weights. No independent verification of exact bibliographic hypotheses or residual-family observations; no refutation of the primary aggregate.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: switches insert a vertex absent from the upper state and the network uses selector-dependent weights. The described unweighted subset-shadow count does not directly bound these cuts absent a further bridge.

claims.statement: For a finite bipartite relation with nonnegative supplies and capacities and uncapacitated allowed arcs, a saturating flow exists exactly when u(X)<=c(N(X)) for every upper-state subset X; the deficit c(N(X))-u(X) is submodular and its global minimizers are closed under union and intersection.
claims.scope: Finite weighted transport instances only. This exact criterion and minimizer structure do not show that any universal tree-derived cut inequalities hold or imply the primary aggregate.
claims.reason: retained: max-flow/min-cut gives the all-subset criterion, while weighted neighborhood coverage is submodular and the supply term is modular. The route also correctly distinguishes the full-set aggregate cut from the stronger all-subset condition.

claims.statement: For a finite group action preserving supplies, capacities and allowed arcs on finite bipartite sides, quotienting by vertex orbits preserves saturating-flow feasibility; this applies to a fixed eligible tree instance when its automorphisms preserve the selector, weights and legal moves.
claims.scope: Finite fixed instances satisfying the invariance hypotheses. It gives no uniform bound over trees, no guarantee of a small quotient, and no tree-wide cut theorem.
claims.reason: retained: each nonempty invariant orbit-pair relation is biregular, so spreading quotient flow uniformly over its edges yields equal per-vertex loads within each orbit. For a fixed ordinary tree its automorphisms preserve original-leaf selector data and the stated move relation.

limitations: No universal tree-derived cut inequalities, complete-sum proof, or complete-sum counterexample was established.
No source computation was replayed; the review checks the general flow and orbit arguments and narrows the literature-scope statement.
The exact cited primary-literature hypotheses and candidate residual-family observation were not independently verified.
No controller verdict or authoritative status is proposed.
